page.summary: Send the Killer a plausible false location when that can open a real escape, rescue or repair rotation.

verdict.recommendation: Choose the decoy whose trigger is ready and whose false location is safely away from the team; leave when the Killer ignores it.
verdict.soloQ: Use a decoy to buy your own route only when it cannot plausibly pull the Killer onto a teammate's live objective.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call the false location and the intended rotation so teammates do not run into the investigation you invited.
verdict.mainWeakness: False notifications have uncertain value, and a Killer who recognizes the tell can stay on the real target.

options.whyItsHere: Throws a false noise and trail after charging outside chase in the Killer's Terror Radius; use it when the landing point creates a safer route.
Fakes a running locker entry and briefly suppresses your trail, creating an immediate route split near a locker.
Sends a noise to a previously touched generator when you enter a locker; plan the marked generator so the lure does not reveal useful team work.
Places a static prop-side decoy after enough repair; useful only when a Killer could plausibly investigate it while you rotate.

weaknesses: Charging or placing a decoy costs position and time, and the Killer may not follow the signal.
killerCounterplay: The Killer can recognize a fake locker or generator cue and keep chasing the actual Survivor or guarding the important objective.
commonMistakes: Throwing Diversion before it is charged or while already in chase.
Marking a generator the team still needs with Red Herring and drawing the Killer to it.
Repeating the same fake location after the Killer stops responding.

opening: Name the real route the decoy will buy; a noise without a follow-up move is only an announcement.

rows.situation: Diversion has charged outside chase and a false landing point draws attention away from the route you need.
rows.action: Throw from cover while crouched and still, then take the opposite safe rotation; skip it if the false cue points toward a teammate.
rows.why: The fake trail and noise matter only if the Killer investigates the wrong place.

rows.situation: A locker sits at a route split and the Killer is tracking your approach.
rows.action: Use Deception while running to fake the entry, then leave along a different route during the brief trail suppression; abandon the trick if the Killer has direct sight of your exit.
rows.why: The decoy suggests a locker search, but it does not conceal a visible Survivor.

rows.situation: A previously touched generator can safely draw the Killer away from a more important route.
rows.action: Enter a locker to trigger Red Herring only after leaving that marked generator; skip it if teammates are repairing or about to return there.
rows.why: The notification goes to the marked generator, which can harm the team if it is the wrong target.

rows.situation: Mirrored Illusion is ready and a suitable prop lies on a plausible Killer patrol route.
rows.action: Place the static decoy beside that prop, then rotate away; do not spend the setup when the Killer already has your position or an urgent rescue needs you.
rows.why: The illusion offers a false visual lead only when the Killer might inspect it.

rows.situation: The Killer ignores repeated fake signals or stays on the real target.
rows.action: Stop investing in decoys and return to a direct escape, rescue or repair route.
rows.why: A lure that changes no Killer decision is pure setup cost.

abortWhen: Do not send a false cue onto a teammate's active objective or rescue route.
Stop repeating a decoy after the Killer demonstrates they will ignore it.
